text: VulkanPipelineStatisticsQueryFeatures.graphicsWorkload

If a pipeline statistics query is created with enabled counters that count graphics work, the command pool from which the associated command buffer is allocated must support the `VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_STATISTICS_BIT` flag. This requirement ensures that the command pool can properly record and manage the specific graphics workload metrics requested by the query. Failure to set this flag when necessary will result in validation errors upon command buffer submission or query creation. Consequently, applications must explicitly enable this capability on the command pool before recording commands that utilize such statistics queries.
vkGetDeviceQueueFamilyProperties, VK_QUEUE_TRANSFER_BIT

The `VK_QUEUE_FAMILY_PROPERTIES` structure reported by `vkGetPhysicalDeviceQueueFamilyProperties` indicates that if the copy parameters are read from device memory, the command pool must be created from a queue family whose index matches the `queueFamilyIndex` specified in the `VkQueueFamilyProperties` structure. Specifically, the rule mandates that the command pool's queue family index must be identical to the queue family index of the device memory from which the copy parameters are read. This restriction ensures that the command buffer is submitted to a queue family capable of accessing the specific device memory region containing the indirect copy parameters. Failure to adhere to this requirement results in undefined behavior or validation errors when submitting the command buffer.
VkFramebuffer creation with render pass subpass viewMask 0b0110 and color attachment VkImageView as 2D array with layerCount 2

The creation of the framebuffer is valid because the framebuffer's color attachment count matches the subpass's color attachment count, and the framebuffer's width and height match the extent of the color attachment image. Furthermore, the framebuffer's layer count matches the layer count of the color attachment image, and the subpass view mask correctly specifies that only the first two layers of the 2D array view are used. Since the framebuffer was created with no flags, the default behavior applies, and no additional requirements regarding the view mask or attachment usage are violated.
vkCmdWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR VkPhysicalDeviceAccelerationStructureFeaturesKHR accelerationStructure disabled

The command vkCmdWriteAccelerationStructuresPropertiesKHR is only valid if the accelerationStructure feature of VkPhysicalDeviceAccelerationStructureFeaturesKHR is enabled at device creation time. Consequently, attempting to record this command with the feature disabled results in undefined behavior. To query compacted sizes, the application must ensure the accelerationStructure feature is enabled before recording any commands that utilize acceleration structures.
VulkanDeviceFeatures halfPrecisionFloatRoundToZero

If the device property `VkPhysicalDeviceProperties::limits.roundToEvenSupported` is not supported for half-precision floats, the shader module must not declare `RoundingModeRoundToEven` for that data type. Consequently, any attempt to use `RoundingModeRoundToEven` with `VkShaderStageFlagBits` targeting half-precision operations will trigger a validation error. The implementation is required to round half-precision floating-point values toward zero instead, and the shader must not rely on the `roundToEven` behavior for these operands.
graphics command buffer record event reset geometry shader stage single-GPU device newer synchronization model enabled geometry shaders not enabled outside render pass

The event reset is invalid because the specified stage, `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_GEOMETRY_SHADER_BIT`, is not a valid stage for the current command buffer; geometry shaders are explicitly disabled on this device, meaning no commands in this buffer can execute at that stage. Furthermore, recording an event reset outside of a render pass is only permitted if the event was previously signaled within a render pass or if the device supports the newer synchronization model with specific constraints that do not apply to a single-GPU device with geometry shaders disabled. Consequently, the event cannot be reset to the signaled state using this stage mask in this context.
vkCreateShaderObjectNV geometry shader feature enable

To create a standalone shader object for the geometry stage, the device must have been created with the `VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_FEATURES_2` structure's `geometryShader` feature enabled. If the device was created without this feature, attempting to create a geometry shader stage will result in validation errors. Consequently, you must either re-create the device with geometry shader support enabled or utilize a pipeline that does not require a dedicated geometry shader stage.
vkCmdDrawIndirect with dynamic vertex input layout

To ensure valid usage when the draw count is read from a buffer, you must record a `VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_RECORDING_STATE` with the `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_DRAW_INDIRECT_BUFFER` flag before issuing the draw command. Additionally, since the pipeline treats only the per-binding vertex stride as dynamic, you must explicitly record the `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VERTEX_INPUT_EXT` state with the appropriate binding index and stride value prior to the draw call. Failing to record these dynamic states will result in a validation error, as the command buffer does not contain the necessary information to resolve the indirect draw count or the specific vertex layout at draw time.
vkBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR, VK_BUILD_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_MODE_UPDATE_KHR, VK_GEOMETRY_TYPE_TRIANGLES_KHR, geometry.triangles.transformData

If the source acceleration structure was last built with a geometry containing a non-NULL `transformData` member, the corresponding geometry in the update operation must also provide a non-NULL `transformData` member. Passing a NULL `transformData` in this context violates the requirement that the update operation must preserve the binding state of existing geometry data. Consequently, this usage is invalid and will result in undefined behavior.
VK_FORMAT_R32_UINT atomic operations storage texel buffer

The operation is invalid because the buffer view lacks the `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_STORAGE_TEXEL_BUFFER_ATOMIC_BIT` feature required for atomic operations on this format. Although the buffer supports storage texel buffer usage, atomic operations are only permitted on formats that explicitly include the atomic feature bit in their buffer features. Consequently, attempting to perform a 32-bit atomic add on a buffer view where this feature is absent violates the valid usage rules for atomic memory operations.
vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer2 VkBufferImageCopy2 imageSubresource aspect mask

The `imageSubresource` aspect mask is invalid because the source image format `VK_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_UNORM` does not support the `VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_DEPTH_BIT` aspect; it must use `VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT` instead. Additionally, the `imageSubresource` structure requires specifying the `mipLevel` and `layer` fields explicitly within the `imageSubresource` member, whereas the provided description implies a single copy operation that must be defined by a single `VkBufferImageCopy2` instance with these fields populated correctly. Finally, ensure that the `imageSubresource` layer count matches the single layer of the source image, as the structure expects a specific layer index rather than a count in the aspect definition.
VK_NV_framebuffer_mixed_samples cluster culling draw call requirements

The usage is invalid because the ClusterCullingHUAWEI stage is not supported by the VK_NV_framebuffer_mixed_samples extension; this extension only defines the `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_COVERAGE_MODULATION_MODE_NV` dynamic state and does not introduce new draw commands or shader stages. Furthermore, the command `vkCmdDrawClusterHUAWEI` is not a valid Vulkan command, as the standard API provides `vkCmdDraw` or `vkCmdDrawIndexed` for issuing draw calls. Consequently, attempting to execute an undefined command within a render pass violates the requirement that all commands must be valid members of the current API version and enabled extensions.
Vulkan specification buffer image copy alignment requirements for depth

If the starting depth of a region plus the copied depth does not reach the end of the subresource's depth, the copied depth must be aligned to 16. This requirement ensures that partial subresource copies are handled consistently with the specification's alignment rules for depth and stencil images. Failure to adhere to this alignment constraint results in undefined behavior during the upload operation.
Vulkan H.264 encode rate control IDR frame interval vs GOP size

If the `idr_interval` parameter is specified as non-zero for H.264 encode rate control, the interval between IDR frames must be greater than or equal to the number of frames in a group of pictures (GOP). Failing to adhere to this constraint results in invalid usage, as the encoder cannot logically skip frames within a single GOP to reach the next IDR boundary. Consequently, applications must ensure that the configured `idr_interval` respects the GOP size defined by the current encoding parameters.
vkCmdSetScissor

The call is invalid because the scissor rectangle's height exceeds the maximum allowed value of `VkExtent3D::MAX_HEIGHT`. According to the Valid Usage rules for `vkCmdSetScissor`, the `height` member of the `VkRect2D` structure must be less than or equal to `VkExtent3D::MAX_HEIGHT`, and a value of 2147483600 violates this constraint.
VkCopyAccelerationStructureInfoKHR dst memory requirements

The memory region of the `dst` acceleration structure that is touched by the copy operation must be bound to device memory. Specifically, the entire range of the `dst` acceleration structure within the specified buffer handle must be backed by device memory that is accessible to the queue family executing the command. If the buffer is partially bound, the copy operation will only succeed for the portion of the acceleration structure that resides within the bound memory range; any part of the structure outside this range must be explicitly bound before the copy is issued. Failure to ensure the full extent of the copied data is backed by device memory will result in undefined behavior.
Vulkan specification cubic filtering indirect non-indexed draw image view restrictions

If the `VK_EXT_multisampled_render_to_texture` extension is not enabled, sampling a multisampled image view with a sampler configured for cubic filtering is undefined behavior in an indirect non-indexed draw. Similarly, attempting to sample an image view with a format that does not support cubic filtering (such as a non-floating-point format or a format lacking the required precision) violates the requirements for this filtering mode. Furthermore, sampling an image view that is not bound to a render pass or is not in the `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_SHADER_READ_ONLY_OPTIMAL` layout when accessed via a shader in this context constitutes a violation of the usage rules for the specified filtering extension.
vkCmdGetAccelerationStructureProperties query pool acceleration structure feature

It is undefined behavior to record a command that writes acceleration structure properties, such as compacted size, into a query pool if the acceleration structure feature was not enabled when the logical device was created. This restriction exists because the underlying acceleration structure state required to compute these properties does not exist in the device's feature set. Consequently, any attempt to execute such a command without the corresponding feature flag enabled will result in validation errors or undefined behavior.
Vulkan subpass dependency color attachment read-only access without feedback loop

If a color target is not configured with VK_ATTACHMENT_LOAD_OP_LOAD and the feedback loop mode is disabled, the image must be treated strictly as a render target for the subsequent draw call within the same subpass. Accessing the image as a read-only resource via a descriptor in a shader stage during this subpass violates the requirement that the image be exclusively used for rendering operations. Consequently, any attempt to sample the image while it remains active as a render target without explicit load operations will trigger a validation error.
VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo subpass, vkCmdNextSubpass, vkCmdDrawMeshTasksEXT

The subpass index specified in VkGraphicsPipelineCreateInfo::subpass defines the subpass index for which the pipeline is valid within the render pass instance. Calling vkCmdNextSubpass transitions the render pass to a different subpass index, rendering the pipeline bound with subpass 0 invalid for subsequent drawing commands. Therefore, you must not call vkCmdDrawMeshTasksEXT while the render pass is in subpass 1 with a pipeline configured for subpass 0. To proceed, you must either rebind a pipeline configured for subpass 1 or transition the render pass back to subpass 0 before issuing the draw call.

The command buffer passed to vkCmdCopyMemoryIndirectKHR must be allocated from a command pool created with a queue family that supports the VK_KHR_copy_memory_indirect extension. Specifically, the device property `VkPhysicalDeviceProperties` does not impose additional restrictions beyond the standard queue family requirements for the graphics, compute, or transfer capabilities defined in the extension's enablement. Consequently, the command pool must be associated with a queue family index that has the `VK_QUEUE_TRANSFER_BIT` bit set if the operation is performed via the transfer queue, or the appropriate capability bit set for graphics or compute queues depending on the specific implementation of the indirect copy. Failure to allocate the command buffer from a command pool backed by a queue family with the necessary capability bits will result in validation errors.
VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_COLOR_WRITE_ENABLE_EXT vkCmdSetColorWriteEnableEXT attachmentCount

The command buffer is invalid because the number of color attachments specified in the `vkCmdSetColorWriteEnableEXT` call must match the number of active color attachments in the subpass. Since the subpass has three active color attachments, the `attachmentCount` parameter must be set to 3, not 2. Additionally, the `colorWriteEnable` feature must be enabled in the instance or device creation parameters, which is already satisfied in your scenario.
vkCmdDrawMultiEXT legacyVertexAttributes VkVertexInputAttributeDescription2EXT format VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32_SFLOAT attribAddress alignment

If the legacyVertexAttributes feature is enabled, the implementation must ensure that the computed attribAddress for a vertex attribute with format VK_FORMAT_R32G32B32_SFLOAT is aligned to a multiple of 12 bytes (the component size of the format). Failure to maintain this alignment constitutes a violation of the valid usage requirements for vkCmdDrawMultiEXT under the legacy vertex attribute path. Developers must explicitly manage the stride and offset calculations to guarantee this alignment is preserved when using the legacy feature set.
VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlInfoKHR idrPeriod gopFrameCount

If `VkVideoEncodeH264RateControlInfoKHR::idrPeriod` is set to a non-zero value, the implementation requires that `idrPeriod` be greater than or equal to `gopFrameCount`. This constraint ensures that the specified IDR period does not exceed the group of pictures boundary defined by the GOP size. Failure to satisfy this condition results in undefined behavior.
VK_IMAGE_CREATE_SPARSE_RESIDENCY_BIT VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR

If the `VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR` flag is specified in `VkImageCreateInfo::tiling`, the `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_SPARSE_RESIDENCY_BIT` flag must not be set in `VkImageCreateInfo::flags`. This is because sparse residency is only supported for images with `VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL` tiling. Attempting to create an image with both `VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR` and `VK_IMAGE_CREATE_SPARSE_RESIDENCY_BIT` set will result in validation layer errors.
VkAccelerationStructureGeometryMicromapDataKHR usage buffer device address

The buffers referenced by the `VkAccelerationStructureGeometryMicromapDataKHR` structure and the device addresses contained within the `VkAccelerationStructureGeometryTrianglesDataKHR` must be created with the `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_BUILD_INPUT_READ_ONLY_BIT_KHR` flag. Additionally, these buffers must not have been created with the `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT` flag, as the micromap data is treated as immutable input during the build process. Failure to set the appropriate read-only usage flag will result in a validation error when `vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresKHR` is called.
vkCmdCopyImage block-compressed format srcOffset.y extent.height srcSubresource

The `extent.height` member of the `VkCopyImageRegion` structure must be a multiple of the texel block height for the source image format if the source subresource is in a block-compressed format. This requirement applies regardless of whether the specified region extends beyond the bottom edge of the subresource, as the copy operation is defined to operate on complete texel blocks. Consequently, attempting to copy a region where `extent.height` does not align with the block height will result in undefined behavior.
Vulkan specification query: micromap device build buffer usage requirements raw data per-triangle descriptor array

The buffers containing the micromap raw data and the per-triangle descriptor array must be created with the `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_MICROMAP_DATA_BIT` and `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_MICROMAP_DESCRIPTOR_BIT` flags, respectively. If a single buffer is used for both purposes, it must be created with both flags combined. Failure to set these usage flags when recording the device build will result in validation errors.
dynamic rendering fragment region rendering flag four-sample attachments per-sample shading minimum shading fraction one half multi-draw

It is undefined behavior to issue a multi-draw call when the fragment region rendering flag is enabled, as this feature requires exclusive control over the render pass instance. Furthermore, enabling per-sample shading with a minimum shading fraction of one half is incompatible with the dynamic rendering fragment region rendering flag, which mandates that all fragments within the specified region be rendered. Consequently, this combination of settings violates the requirements for dynamic rendering and will result in undefined behavior.
Vulkan buffer destruction requirements after texel view submission without host allocator

The buffer must remain valid until the command buffer recording is finished or until the GPU has completed all operations referencing the buffer, whichever occurs later. Destroying the buffer immediately after submitting work that reads from it violates this requirement, as the GPU may still be accessing the underlying memory. Consequently, this usage is invalid and will result in undefined behavior if the GPU attempts to read from the destroyed buffer.
taskEXT_mesh_workgroup_count private

The built-in variable that reports the number of launched mesh workgroups must reside in private per-invocation storage, as it is defined specifically for use within the task shader's execution context. Placing this variable in shared or global storage would violate the requirement that the count reflects the outcome of the current task invocation without interfering with other tasks. Consequently, attempts to declare this built-in in any storage class other than private will trigger a validation error.
VkBlitImageInfo2 dstImage format features VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_SRC_BIT VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_DST_BIT

The `dstImage` member of a `VkBlitImageInfo2` structure must have a format that supports the `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_DST_BIT` feature. If the format of `dstImage` lacks this feature, the operation is invalid regardless of whether the source image format supports `VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_SRC_BIT`. Consequently, attempting to use such a destination image in a blit operation will result in validation layer errors.
vkCmdDispatchIndirect buffer memory requirements

The buffer bound to the `VkBuffer` parameter of `vkCmdDispatchIndirect` must be bound to memory that is accessible from the device queue family used for the command recording. If the buffer was created without the `VK_BUFFER_CREATE_SPARSE_BINDING_BIT` flag, the memory backing the buffer must be allocated with `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_DEVICE_LOCAL_BIT` or `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT` and `VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT` as appropriate for the access pattern, ensuring the memory is not sparse. Specifically, the memory must reside in a memory heap that is compatible with the device's requirements for non-sparse buffers, preventing any sparse memory access violations during the indirect dispatch operation.
Vulkan specification indirect command buffer memory binding requirements for compute dispatch

The buffer containing the workgroup counts must be bound to the pipeline via `vkCmdBindDescriptorSet` with a descriptor type of `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER` or `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_BUFFER_DYNAMIC`. Furthermore, the memory associated with this buffer must be accessible to the compute shader stage at the point of the indirect dispatch command, ensuring that the read occurs within the valid lifetime of the buffer binding. If the buffer is created with `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT`, it must also satisfy the requirement that its memory is not used for any other purpose that would conflict with the storage access during the dispatch.
VkCommandPool creation flags required for VK_QUERY_TYPE_PIPELINE_STATISTICS graphics operations

The VkCommandPool of commandBuffer must support the VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_TRANSIENT_BIT flag if the queryPool is created with VK_QUERY_POOL_CREATE_TRANSIENT_BIT, or it must support the default flags if the queryPool is created without that flag. Specifically, the commandPool must support the VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT queue family index associated with the graphics pipeline stage being queried. Additionally, the commandBuffer must be recorded within a command pool that has been created with a level of VK_COMMAND_POOL_CREATE_RESET_COMMAND_BUFFER_BIT or higher to ensure proper command buffer management for pipeline statistics queries.
VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_GEOMETRY_SHADER_BIT with geometry shader disabled

If synchronization2 is enabled, recording `vkCmdResetEvent2` with `VK_PIPELINE_STAGE_2_GEOMETRY_SHADER_BIT` is valid only if the geometry shader stage is enabled in the pipeline; otherwise, the pipeline stage is invalid for the current command buffer. Since the geometry shader stage is not enabled in this scenario, the usage is invalid. Furthermore, resetting an event outside a render pass is permitted, but the specified pipeline stage must correspond to an active stage in the executing pipeline. Consequently, this usage violates the requirement that the pipeline stage must be enabled when the geometry shader stage is specified.
Vulkan coverage reduction mode dynamic discard indirect mesh task draw

If the coverage reduction mode feature is enabled and the pipeline state object leaves the coverage reduction mode dynamic, the application must ensure that no indirect mesh task draw commands are issued while the coverage reduction mode is set to discard rasterization. Specifically, when reading the draw count from a buffer for an indirect mesh task draw, the application must verify that the draw count does not exceed the maximum allowed for the current coverage reduction mode setting before recording the command. Failure to align the draw count with the active coverage reduction mode may result in undefined behavior or incorrect rasterization results.
vkCmdDrawIndirectCount with VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VERTEX_INPUT_BINDING_STRIDE

If the pipeline enables VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VERTEX_INPUT_BINDING_STRIDE, the application must record calls to vkCmdSetVertexInputEXT in the command buffer prior to vkCmdDrawIndirectCount to specify the stride for each vertex input binding. Failure to record these calls before the draw command will result in undefined behavior or a validation error if the stride is not explicitly defined for the active bindings. Note that VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_VERTEX_INPUT_EXT is required to set the stride values, even when the pipeline itself supports the dynamic state, as the command buffer must explicitly provide the stride data for each binding.
Vulkan specification render pass framebuffer creation multiple view subpass single color attachment layer mismatch

A framebuffer is valid only if all its attachments have matching width, height, and layer count, and if the subpass description references attachments that are compatible with the framebuffer's attachment descriptions. In your case, since the framebuffer has a single layer while the color view covers two array layers, the layer counts do not match, rendering the framebuffer invalid. Furthermore, a subpass cannot write to a single attachment that is described as covering multiple array layers within the same framebuffer attachment description without explicit handling of array layers in the subpass description. Therefore, this configuration violates the requirement that the number of layers in the framebuffer attachment must equal the number of layers referenced in the subpass for that attachment.
color attachment remapping distinct index dynamic rendering

When remapping color attachments to shader input attachment indices for local reads in dynamic rendering, each color attachment that is actually mapped must be assigned a distinct index. Assigning the same index to multiple active color attachments violates the requirement that input attachments within a single render pass must have unique indices. Consequently, the implementation will generate a validation error if duplicate indices are provided for mapped color attachments.
VK_IMG_filter_cubic VK_EXT_filter_cubic VK_FILTER_CUBIC_EXT VkImageViewType

If the device supports VK_IMG_filter_cubic but the VK_EXT_filter_cubic extension is not enabled, using a VK_FILTER_CUBIC_EXT sampler with an image view of type VK_IMAGE_TYPE_1D or VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D is invalid. The Vulkan specification mandates that when VK_EXT_filter_cubic is not enabled, cubic filtering is only permitted for image views of type VK_IMAGE_TYPE_3D. Consequently, attempting to sample a 1D or 2D image view with a cubic sampler in this configuration violates the valid usage rules for the sampler.
vkCmdBuildAccelerationStructuresIndirectKHR scratchData deviceAddress alignment

The `scratchData.deviceAddress` must point to a location within the buffer that is explicitly marked with the `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_DEVICE_ADDRESS_BIT` usage flag, not merely a region with sufficient size or alignment. Additionally, the buffer containing the scratch data must have the `VK_BUFFER_USAGE_STORAGE_BUFFER_BIT` usage flag set if it is intended to be written to by the acceleration structure build process, as the indirect build mode requires write access to the scratch space. Ensure that the `dstAccelerationStructure` binding and the `scratchData` binding are correctly associated with their respective pipeline stages and that no other conflicting usages prevent the driver from mapping the device address correctly.
VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_LINE_STIPPLE_ENABLE_EXT VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_EXT vkCmdDrawMultiIndexedEXT stippledRectangularLines

If `stippledLineEnable` is set to `VK_TRUE` and `lineRasterizationMode` is set to `VK_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_RECTANGULAR`, the application must ensure that `stippledRectangularLines` is enabled prior to calling `vkCmdDrawMultiIndexedEXT`. Failure to enable `stippledRectangularLines` while using this specific combination of dynamic states constitutes a violation of the validation requirements for the `VK_EXT_line_stippling` extension. Consequently, the driver will report a validation error if these conditions are not met before issuing the draw command.
Vulkan dynamic state per-attachment color write enable toggle indirect non-indexed draw

If per-attachment color write toggling is enabled on the device, the pipeline must specify the same set of active color attachments for which the write toggle is enabled in the dynamic state; therefore, enabling the toggle for only two of the three active color attachments in the subpass is invalid. Furthermore, the write toggle must be set for every active color attachment in the subpass when rasterization is not discarded, as the specification requires that all active color attachments have their corresponding write toggles enabled prior to the draw call. Consequently, failing to enable the write toggle for the third active color attachment violates the valid usage requirements for per-attachment color write toggling.
VkBufferView lifetime requirements after vkQueueSubmit

This usage is invalid because the buffer is destroyed while a command buffer submitted to the queue is still executing and accessing the buffer via the associated buffer view. The Vulkan specification requires that a buffer remain valid for the entire duration of any command buffer that references it, including the time between `vkQueueSubmit` and the completion of the work on the queue. Destroying the buffer before the queue has finished processing the submission violates the requirement that the buffer must not be destroyed while it is in use by the GPU.
VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer feature enablement for vkCmdBindIndexBuffer2 with VK_NULL_HANDLE

The feature `VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer` must be enabled to allow the use of `VK_NULL_HANDLE` as the buffer parameter in `vkCmdBindIndexBuffer2`. This extension introduces the concept of descriptor buffers, where a null handle signifies that the index buffer is provided via a descriptor buffer rather than a standard memory object. Consequently, attempting to bind a null handle without this feature enabled will result in a validation error. Ensure that the instance or device extension is enabled before invoking this command with a null buffer.
vkCreateGraphicsPipelines graphics pipeline library vertex input interface

The vertex input interface state is not correctly inherited because the pipeline library passed in `pLibraries` was created with `VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_LIBRARY_BIT_KHR` but does not explicitly contain the vertex input interface state required by the `VK_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_LIBRARY_VERTEX_INPUT_INTERFACE_BIT_EXT` flag. When creating a pipeline with `VK_PIPELINE_CREATE_LIBRARY_BIT_KHR`, the driver expects that any state bits set in the create info (such as `VK_GRAPHICS_PIPELINE_LIBRARY_VERTEX_INPUT_INTERFACE_BIT_EXT`) are fully satisfied by the union of states present in the provided libraries; however, a library created solely with the library bit does not automatically populate the specific interface state needed unless it was explicitly built with that state. To resolve this, you must ensure the library referenced in `pLibraries` was created with the corresponding vertex input state included, or create a separate library containing only the vertex input interface state and pass it alongside the main pipeline library. Additionally, verify that the vertex input interface state in the main pipeline's `pVertexInputState` matches the interface defined in the library, as mismatches can lead to validation errors even if the flags are set correctly.
Vulkan 1.3 VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_MEMORY_BARRIER_INFO bind command null buffer handle feature enable

To bind an index buffer with a null handle using the newer command that accepts a size parameter, the device must support the `VK_KHR_push_descriptor` extension or the application must have explicitly enabled the `VK_EXT_descriptor_buffer` extension with the `VK_DESCRIPTOR_BUFFER_ALLOW_NULL` feature. If this feature is not enabled, passing a null handle in this context will result in a validation error. Consequently, developers must ensure the appropriate device feature flag is active before utilizing the null handle optimization for index buffers.
VK_EXT_line_stippling

The use of `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_LINE_STIPPLE_ENABLE_EXT` and `VK_DYNAMIC_STATE_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_EXT` requires the `lineStippling` device feature to be enabled. Additionally, setting `lineRasterizationMode` to `VK_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_BRESENHAM` necessitates the `lineRasterizationModeBresenham` device feature. If either of these features is not enabled on the physical device, the command buffer recording will fail validation. Ensure that both `lineStippling` and `lineRasterizationModeBresenham` are present in the enabled device features before recording the draw command.
legacy_vertex_attribute_compatibility multi_draw vertex_attribute_format three 32-bit float components address alignment

If the legacy vertex attribute compatibility feature is enabled, a multi-draw operation reading a vertex attribute in an ordinary non-packed format composed of three 32-bit float components requires the computed address of that attribute to be aligned to the size of one component (32 bits). Failure to satisfy this alignment requirement constitutes a validation error. This rule ensures consistent memory access patterns for legacy hardware that may not support unaligned loads for such attribute layouts. Developers must ensure the stride and offset calculations result in an address divisible by 4 bytes before issuing the draw command.
Vulkan dynamic rendering single layer color attachment multisample resolve custom resolve mode

When using a custom resolve mode, the multisampled color attachment must be resolved to a single-sampled attachment of the same format and layout, but the source and destination views must not be identical; specifically, the resolve operation requires the source to be multisampled and the destination to be single-sampled, which is violated if the resolved view is treated as the same logical attachment without a distinct underlying image or if the resolve operation is attempted on a view that does not strictly adhere to the multisample-to-single-sample transition semantics defined for the custom resolve mode. Additionally, ensure that the render area fits within the dimensions of the multisampled attachment and that no other rendering flags conflict with the custom resolve configuration. If the custom resolve mode is enabled, the pipeline must guarantee that the resolve operation occurs between distinct sampling levels, and the layout of the resolved view must be compatible with the immediate post-resolve state expected by the pipeline.
vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect shader objects mesh shader VK_NULL_HANDLE VK_SHADER_STAGE_MESH_BIT_EXT tessellationShader geometryShader disabled
